subject: paediatrics
title: Neonatal respiratory disorders: RDS, TTN, MAS and air leaks

steps.tx: **Respiratory distress syndrome** affects preterm babies who lack enough **surfactant** to keep their alveoli open. The chest film in this image shows ground glass shadowing with air bronchograms through the stiff lungs. The baby grunts, flares the nostrils and shows chest retractions while working hard to breathe. Early continuous positive airway pressure and thin catheter surfactant reduce the need for prolonged ventilation.
steps.say: The chest film can show the pale and grainy lungs of a very early baby. Dark air filled tubes stand out against the stiff and under expanded lung tissue. The baby will grunt and pull the chest inward with every difficult breath. Missing surfactant makes each tiny air sac collapse at the end of breathing. Early pressure support and timely surfactant help the lungs stay open.

vis.alt: Chest X-ray of a preterm infant with RDS showing ground glass opacities and air bronchograms. Clinical signs include grunting, nasal flaring, and retractions.
vis.caption: RDS: Ground glass X-ray, air bronchograms, grunting, flaring, retracting

steps.tx: **Transient tachypnoea** affects a term baby after caesarean birth when lung fluid clears slowly from the airways. The baby breathes fast for some hours and usually recovers within 24 to 72 hours with support. **Meconium aspiration** affects a post term baby who passes meconium before birth and inhales the stained fluid. An air leak such as **pneumothorax** needs urgent drainage when it compresses the lung.
steps.say: A term baby may breathe fast because birth fluid leaves the lungs slowly. This problem will usually settle within one to three days with oxygen and observation. A baby who passes stool before birth can inhale that thick material deeply. The inhaled material blocks small airways and inflames the lung tissue badly. Air that escapes outside the lung can compress it and needs urgent release.

steps.tx: In **persistent pulmonary hypertension** blood shunts right to left through the ductus and foramen ovale, so **prepostductal** saturation differs by over 10. Inhaled **nitric oxide** dilates the pulmonary vessels selectively and improves oxygen levels. A diaphragmatic hernia pushes bowel into the chest, and the team avoids bag and mask ventilation that inflates that bowel. Delayed surgery after stabilisation gives a better outcome than rushed repair.
steps.say: Blood can bypass the lungs when pressure inside the lung vessels stays very high. The saturation measured before the ductus then differs clearly from the value after it. A gas that dilates only the lung vessels can improve oxygen without dropping body pressure. Bowel inside the chest from a hernia must not be inflated by mask ventilation. Stabilising the baby first gives the surgical team a safer operating window.

steps.tx: This film shows **bowel loops in the chest** with a **scaphoid abdomen**, which points to a diaphragmatic hernia in a newborn. The inset shows right to left shunting through the ductus and foramen ovale in **persistent pulmonary hypertension**. Inhaled nitric oxide appears as one treatment that lowers pulmonary vascular resistance. For the exam, avoid bag and mask ventilation here because it inflates bowel and worsens compression.
steps.say: The main film shows loops of bowel sitting inside the left side of the chest. The belly looks sunken because much of its normal content has moved upward. The small diagram shows blood bypassing the lungs through fetal channels after birth. That bypass causes severe low oxygen that responds poorly to oxygen alone. A selective lung vessel dilator can help while the team stabilises the baby.

steps.tx: **Apnoea of prematurity** causes repeated pauses in breathing, and **caffeine** reduces those spells in preterm babies. Continuous positive airway pressure splints the airway open, while transfusion helps when anaemia contributes. The team keeps saturation targets near **90 to 95** in preterm babies to protect the eyes and lungs. Regular eye, hearing and growth checks complete the follow up plan.
steps.say: Early babies often pause their breathing because the breathing control centre remains immature. A stimulant medicine reduces the number and severity of those pauses. Gentle airway pressure keeps the small air passages open during sleep. Low blood count can worsen the spells and may need transfusion support. Careful oxygen targets protect the developing eyes while the baby grows steadily.
